title: High-content live-cell multiplex screen for chemogenomic compound annotation based on nuclear morphology
protocol: Wash the cells in a T75 flask once with 5 mL PBS buffer.
Detach the cells using 3 mL trypsin.
Determine the concentration and viability of the cells using trypan blue 0.4% solution.
Mix 10 μL cells and 10 μL trypan blue and add to a counting slide for automated cell counting.
Put the counting slide into the TC20 Automated Cell Counter.
Count the unstained (live) and stained (dead) cells.
Wait till the results appear on the Cell Counter screen.
Dilute the cells to 3 × 10^4 cells/mL and a final volume of 16 mL/384 well plate or cell concentration determined in your preliminary experiment for confluence ranging from 50%–90% after 48 h.
Mix 57 μL of a 16.23 μM stock of Hoechst33342.
Add 8 μL of a stock of BioTracker™ 488 Green Microtubule Cytoskeleton Dye.
Mix 12 μL of a 100 μM stock of Mitotracker red.
Combine 93 μL of a stock of Annexin V Alexa Fluor 680 conjugate with the mixture.
Gently mix the cell suspension by inverting it.
Transfer 50 μL of the cell suspension containing fluorescent dyes to the corresponding wells of the 384 well plate using a multichannel pipet and a reagent reservoir.
Pipette 100 μL PBS buffer or water into the outer wells as indicated.
Remove any air bubbles that may have been formed during pipetting.
Incubate the plate for 18–24 h at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Put a lid on the plate prepared in steps 3–6 and leave it for 30 min under the cell culture hood at room temperature to allow reattachment of the U-2 OS cells to the plate.
Switch on the CQ1 microscope and the separate laser module.
Wait 3 minutes for the laser to heat up.
Ensure that the environmental controls regulating temperature, CO2 partial pressure, and water reservoirs are functioning.
Set the temperature of the CQ1 microscope to 37°C.
Set the partial pressure of CO2 to 5%.
Set the humidity to 100%.
Place the prepared plate in the CQ1 microscope.
Open the imaging software using either the associated automation unit or manual handling.
Open the measuring protocol for imaging.
Assess if the measuring protocol provides focused images of sufficient intensity in all channels.
Choose approximately 10 wells spread randomly over the entire plate.
Test if the focus area and channel parameters can detect cells and fluorescent signals of different channels.
Measure the plate once with non-treated cells using the described protocol.
Put the plate into an incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2 until compound treatment.
Use the Echo® source plate prepared in step 7 to add compounds to your plate.
Open the “Pick list” program in the Echo® 550 liquid handler system on your computer.
Select “new” to create a new protocol.
Enter for the source- and destination plate the right Sample Plate Format (384LDV) and the right Sample Plate Type.
For DMSO as solvent, use 384LDV_DMSO as plate type.
Import your picklist, which should be saved as “.csv” on your local storage space.
Check your layout again on “plate preview.”
After adding the compounds, centrifuge the plate for 3 min at 100 × g.
Place the treated cells plate in the CQ1 microscope.
Open the measuring protocol used for the acquisition of non-treated cells (see image acquisition of non-treated cells).
Test the measuring protocol with the inserted cell plate.
Scan 3–5 wells to test if the focus area of the initial baseline measurement is still appropriate.
Define Scan Schedule and Frequency for testing.
Measure the plate 12 hours, 24 hours, and 48 hours after compound treatment.
Use the CellPathfinder software for image analysis.
Open the CellPathfinder software.
Follow the protocol "CellPathfinder_AnalysisProtocol_U2OS_Multiplex" for U-2 OS cells analysis.
Adapt the protocol for different cell types and magnifications as necessary.
Evaluate the resulting data and processed images to obtain phenotypical annotation of each tested compound.
Open the folder containing CQ1 measurement data.
Select the data you want to analyze.
Convert the selected CQ1 image data by clicking “convert”.
Load the analysis protocol for U-2 OS cells from the Protocol tab.
Click on the process buttons at the top of the operation window to navigate through parameters step-by-step.
Open the “Channels” section in the protocol.
Set channel 1 (CH1) for Hoechst33342 with excitation/emission at 405/447/60 nm.
Set channel 2 (CH2) for BioTracker™ 488 Green Microtubule Cytoskeleton Dye with excitation/emission at 488/525/50 nm.
Set channel 3 (CH3) for MitoTracker red with excitation/emission at 561/617/73 nm.
Set channel 4 (CH4) for Annexin V with excitation/emission at 640/685/40 nm.
Configure channel 5 (CH5) as brightfield, DCP Fluor Type Simple Mode, Contrast 0.06.
Configure channel 6 (CH6) as brightfield, DCP Phase Type Simple Mode, Contrast 0.04.
Pre-analyze your data in the CellPathfinder software.
Process images and detect objects for the pre-analysis step.
Select wells with reference compounds important for training ML-based functions.
Include non-treated cells in the pre-analysis for a comprehensive dataset.
Ensure correct detection of cell bodies and nuclei in 5–10 example wells.
Click on “Pre-Analyze” and select specific wells (N5 to N12 and O5 to O12).
Train the ML based gating algorithm after successful pre-analysis.
Open the “Gate” section for training the ML-based functions.
Detect cell bodies and cell nuclei using the software pre-analysis.
Train the machine learning algorithm based on reference compounds.
Analyze the whole plate and all time points using the tree principle.
Gate cells into categories of Hoechst High Intensity Objects or normal cells.
Gated “Normal” cells are further classified as healthy nucleus, pyknosed nucleus, or fragmented nucleus.
Cells with a pyknosed nucleus are gated further into mitosis or apoptosis.
Investigate phenotypic properties of interest by gating cells showing a healthy nucleus into tubulin effect or tubulin normal.
Evaluate mitochondrial mass increased or mitochondrial mass normal based on gated cells.
Determine membrane permeabilized or membrane intact status for the cells.
Use reference compounds with known phenotypes to train the machine learning-based analysis.
Select individual cells (minimum 10 images) for each gating step as examples for the gating phenotype.
Train a scientist or use provided example images for selecting cells.
Save the trained ML-based analysis.
Run the saved analysis on all wells containing reference compounds.
Compare results of reference compound treated wells to ensure consistency and no deviation by more than 10% from known biological mode of action.
Analyze the whole plate once the machine learning-based analysis is well trained.
Open the metadata template file named “metadata_template.xlsx”.
Fill all sheets in the metadata template.
Describe your basic experimental setup in the sheet “experiments”.
Describe all time points for which you acquired images in the sheet “imaging campaigns”.
Indicate the path to cq1 analysis data in the column “cq1 analysis available in folder” on the sheet “imaging campaigns”.
Fill the sheet “exclude from file list” if you want to deposit your data and omit individual processed images.
Describe all compounds used in the experiment in the sheet “compounds”, including their chemical structure formula as SMILES.
List all specific batches of the compounds used in the sheet “compound batches”.
Create (or rename) a compound map sheet.
Fill out information about the concentration of the compound in individual wells.
Specify the experimental type for each well as “blank”, “cells only”, “chemogenomic candidate”, or “control”.
Optional: Fill out “raw data available in zip file” and “processed images available in folder” if you want to deposit your data.
Save the file under a name denoted “METADATA_FILENAME”.
Perform automated checks on the file by opening Anaconda Prompt.
Enter “python quality_control_of_excel_file.py METADATA_FILENAME”.
Open the Anaconda Prompt.
Execute python create_filelist_raw_cq1.py METADATA_FILENAME.
Check the Prompt for error messages and act on them if applicable.
Execute python create_filelist_processed_images_c1.py METADATA_FILENAME.
Check the Prompt for error messages and act on them if applicable.
Create two Study Components in your submission to BioImage Archive.
Use filelist_raw_data_cq1.xlsx to populate a Study Component about the raw data.
Use filelist_cq1_processed_images_all_experiments.xlsx to populate a separate study component about the processed images.
Submit your study in BioImage Archive.
Open the file "cq1_evaluated_all.xlsx" located in the root path.
Manually inspect the results within the file.
